question: Has road safety for pedestrians in Brooklyn gotten better since 2013? Make a chart suitable for a local news story and summarize the findings.

options.metric: Annual pedestrian casualties = sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured plus number_of_pedestrians_killed across Brooklyn crashes.
options.reason: It captures the total annual burden of pedestrian harm by combining injuries and deaths into one trend.
options.answer: Pedestrian casualties in Brooklyn fell from 3,671 in 2013 to 2,874 in 2025, but rose from a low of 1,798 in 2020.
options.interpretation: For police-reported Brooklyn crashes (borough matched after trimming whitespace and ignoring case) in complete calendar years 2013–2025, this absolute count sums pedestrians injured and killed per crash; it fell 22% from 3,671 in 2013 to 2,874 in 2025, after a low of 1,798 in 2020. It is a defensible measure of the annual burden of pedestrian harm, but it does not answer whether risk per walking trip or distance improved because the file has no pedestrian-exposure denominator. The check found 9,700 of 483,501 post-2013 Brooklyn crash rows (2.0%) were in partial 2026 through June 11, so those rows were excluded; among the checked population, 0 borough/date values and 0 injury/death values were missing, so complete-year rows were retained.

options.metric: Annual pedestrians killed = sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed across Brooklyn crashes.
options.reason: Deaths are the most severe pedestrian outcome and provide a focused measure of fatal safety.
options.answer: Pedestrian deaths in Brooklyn increased from 30 in 2013 to 39 in 2025, although the yearly counts fluctuate substantially.
options.interpretation: For police-reported Brooklyn crashes (borough matched after trimming whitespace and ignoring case) in complete calendar years 2013–2025, this absolute count sums pedestrians killed per crash; it increased from 30 in 2013 to 39 in 2025, with a low of 17 in 2020. Deaths are a defensible focused measure of the most severe outcome, but they leave nonfatal injuries out and do not establish risk per walking trip or distance because the file has no pedestrian-exposure denominator. The check found 9,700 of 483,501 post-2013 Brooklyn crash rows (2.0%) were in partial 2026 through June 11, so those rows were excluded; among the checked population, 0 borough/date values and 0 death values were missing, so complete-year rows were retained.

answer:
1. Pedestrian casualties (injuries plus deaths) fell from 3,671 in 2013 to 2,874 in 2025, though they have risen since 2020; [chart](out/option_1.png).
2. Pedestrian deaths increased from 30 in 2013 to 39 in 2025, with substantial year-to-year fluctuations; [chart](out/option_2.png).
